title: Integral as arithmetic average over Boolean inputs
statement:
Let $f \colon \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n \to \bbr$ be any real-valued function on the $n$-bit Boolean inputs. Then, integrating $f$ against the uniform probability measure on the $2^n$ inputs,
\[
  \int f \;=\; \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x} f(x),
\]
so that the integral equals the arithmetic average of the values $f(x)$ taken over all $x \in \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is any real-valued function on the n-bit Boolean inputs
replaced:
For any $f : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n \to \mathbb{R}$, the integral against the uniform
distribution satisfies
\[
  \int x,\, f(x) \;=\; \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x} f(x).
\]
